guide.description: A glob like *.txt lets you refer to a file by pattern instead of typing its exact name. The shell expands it against the current directory before the command ever sees it — if exactly one file matches, that's the file that gets read. Not every command expands globs here: head, tail, wc, grep, sed, awk, sort, uniq, and cut all do — cat and ls take their argument literally. Shell Fundamentals assumes you already know ls, pwd, cat, and the pipes/text-tools from the Text Tools course — this course is about working faster.
